  "claim": "recover_json_object skips fenced candidates whose strict parse fails, so it never applies the documented repeated-key last-wins recovery to objects inside code fences; a fenced object with repeated keys can therefore lose to a later top-level object.",
  "expected": "For an input containing a fenced duplicate-key JSON object and then a later top-level object, recover_json_object should score the last object inside the fence, resolving the repeated key last-wins. For example, it should return {'a': 2} from the reproducer (so k_recovery would return '{\"a\":2}').",
  "observed": "It skips the fenced duplicate-key candidate because the source sets parsed = None whenever the pool is the fenced pool, then falls through to the top-level pool and returns the later top-level object {'b': 3} (so k_recovery would return '{\"b\":3}').",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\":1,\"a\":2}\n```\n{\"b\":3}",
  "source_basis": "Documentation for recover_json_object: 'The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text' and 'A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable'. Source contradicts this with: 'parsed = None if pool is fenced else _loads_last_wins(candidate.strip())'.",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Inputs where a code fence contains a JSON object with repeated keys and a later top-level strict JSON object exists outside any fence.",
  "uncertainty": "Assumes loads_strict rejects duplicate keys, as the recover_json_object documentation states; if it did not, this particular input would parse strictly and the defect would not appear."
